registeredBy: the item-quality harness builder (branch feat/item-eval), before the first scored run
decision: A metric meets its threshold when its point estimate does. Every rate is reported with n and a Wilson 95% interval; a met threshold whose interval crosses it is reported as 'met, not established at 95%'. A missed threshold is reported in the same table, never dropped. Changing a threshold after a run is a new registration with its own date.

parse.population: model responses, excluding planted unparseable responses
parse.definition: The response parses against the pack's JSON schema (zod, strict).

verbatimQuote.population: sources of stored items (including code-derived cards)
verbatimQuote.definition: The stored quote equals the stored resource text sliced at the stored offsets.

modelQuoteFidelity.definition: Diagnostic, no threshold: the model's own quote occurs verbatim (whitespace collapsed) in the passage it cites, among the passages it was sent.

singleKey.population: multiple-choice and true/false items the model wrote
singleKey.definition: Exactly one option is keyed (MC) or the statement's truth is set (TF), before any check.

flawRate.definition: At least one cue-flaw rule of packages/learning/src/flaws.ts (the pipeline's stage 4) fires.

plantedCatch.population: planted defects that code can catch (cases/planted.json, requiresJudge false), plus planted unparseable responses
plantedCatch.definition: The defect never reaches a stored item: it is dropped, or (answer leaks) the stored item hides its answer; an unparseable response is retried to a parsed one. Offline only.

falseDrop.population: items the offline model wrote (correct and grounded by construction), excluding drops by the cue-flaw rules (counted in flawRate) and near-duplicate drops (counted in duplicate)
falseDrop.definition: A correct, grounded item dropped by a correctness or grounding check (schema, quote, executed, tags, explanation, policy). Offline only: live items carry no labels.

duplicate.definition: Dropped as a near-duplicate (trigram Jaccard >= 0.8 against an earlier item of the course), or stored while a near-duplicate of an earlier stored item of the same scope.

repeatZeroTokens.population: repeat requests of a completed pack with unchanged content
repeatZeroTokens.definition: The repeat is a cache hit, costs 0 tokens and makes no model call.

subjectFit.population: whole-course runs of courses whose subject family code knows; offline, synthetic courses only (the offline model extracts too few facts from OCW text to hold a family's mix)
subjectFit.definition: The stored items meet every rule in subjectRules for the course's family.

promptSubject.population: model calls for courses whose subject family code knows
promptSubject.definition: The prompt sent carries the course's subject profile line (plan D35, D52).

moduleCoverage.population: materials in whole-course scopes; offline, synthetic courses only (same reason)
moduleCoverage.definition: The material is cited by at least one stored item of the quiz and cards runs together.

goldTopicCoverage.population: gold topics of the synthetic courses (cases/*.json), whole-course scope
goldTopicCoverage.definition: A stored item's source span overlaps the gold topic's quote. Gold topics are builder-written, not independent.

subjectRules.languages: Vocabulary cards in both directions (at least one reverse pair); cloze cards present; no numeric quiz items.
subjectRules.math, physical_science, engineering: Numeric items are at least 25% of stored quiz items; at least one numeric item recomputed by code; at least 90% of the numeric items the model wrote are kept.
subjectRules.computing: Term cards, cloze cards and multiple-choice items present.
subjectRules.humanities, social_science, arts: Term cards and cloze cards present; every numeric item is a year (1000-2100) or a figure recomputed by code.

amendments.after: the first offline baseline run (harness at commit 10eeb2d plus the uncommitted harness)
amendments.change: falseDrop now excludes cue-flaw drops (already counted in flawRate); subjectFit and moduleCoverage count synthetic courses only in offline runs.
amendments.reason: The offline model can write items with cue flaws (a key longer than distractors when the course has few same-kind terms); dropping those is the rule working, not a false drop. The offline model's regex extraction from OCW captions is sparse, so OCW subject fit and coverage measured the offline model, not the app. Thresholds are unchanged.
